Pre-fill the values that repeat on every gift in this batch.


Click Set Batch Defaults in the highlights bar above. Enter the fields you don't want to retype for every entry — campaign, gift designation, payment method, stewardship contact, gift received date, whatever applies to the whole batch — and save.


Defaults apply to entries added after you save them. Rows already in the batch keep the values you originally typed. You can reopen Set Batch Defaults any time before processing to change or clear them, and any default can still be overridden field-by-field on an individual entry.

Add each gift as a Gift Entry row on the Gift Entries tab.


Use New Gift Entry in the highlights bar above to open the grid. The template on this batch decides which fields you see and their order — fields you pre-filled in step 1 come in pre-populated, but you can still override any of them per row.


Enter gifts in any order and over multiple sittings — the batch stays open until you process it. If you have gift data in a spreadsheet, use the Import from CSV option to upload rows instead of typing each one.


As you add entries, the Total Gift Count and Total Batch Amount in the highlights bar rise. Compare them against the Estimated Gift Count and Expected Value of Gifts in Batch you set on the batch header — those are your reconciliation targets.

Simulate processing to catch errors before you commit.


Click Batch Dry Run in the highlights bar above. Fundraising re-validates every gift entry against the current state of your data — donor lookups, designations, campaigns, required fields — but does not create or update any records. Refresh the page to watch the status move from In Progress to a result.


When the dry run finishes, review the Gift Entries tab below. The Failed Gift Entries list surfaces every row that would fail; the Gift Processing Result column explains why. Fix each row (edit the entry, resolve the donor, correct the designation, etc.) and re-run the dry run until it's clean.


Also check the count and value reconciliation: if the dry run flags that Total Gift Count doesn't match Estimated Gift Count, or Total Batch Amount doesn't match Expected Value of Gifts in Batch, either add the missing entries, correct the estimates on the batch header, or clear Total Gift Value Match to skip that check.


You can't add or edit entries while a dry run is running — wait for it to finish. Once it's done, entries are editable again.

Commit the batch to create the gift records.


Once your dry run comes back clean, click Process Batch in the highlights bar above. Fundraising creates a Gift Transaction for every entry, plus Gift Transaction Designations (one per allocation if a gift is split), Gift Soft Credits (one per soft-credit recipient), and new donor Accounts where the entry references someone not already in the org.


Refresh the page to watch Status. When it lands, expect one of three outcomes:


Processed — every entry succeeded. Review the Successful Gift Entries list below and the Processed Results section on the Details tab. Entries are now locked from further edits.


Partially Processed — some entries succeeded and some failed. Successful entries created their records; failed ones did not. Open the Failed Gift Entries list, read the Gift Processing Result on each, correct the underlying issue, then click Process Batch again — Fundraising only reprocesses the entries that haven't succeeded yet.


Failed — nothing committed. Fix the surfaced errors and reprocess.


A single batch can process up to 50,000 gift entries. If your batch is nearing that ceiling, split it into two batches with the same template and defaults.
